title: feat(provision.declastruct): --org slot and --expect member|management account guard
description:
## .what

two flags on `provision.declastruct`, plus a guard skill, so a repo with more than one keyrack org can provision a member account safely. a consumer (rhachet-roles-nheuron) built them locally as `provision.member`, `provision.root`, and `aws.caller.get --expect`; they should live here.

1. **`--org <org>`** — the keyrack org slot to unlock and source (`keyrack unlock|source --org`). today `--env prep` always sources the repo's default org, so a wish for another org's account plans against the default org's AWS_PROFILE.
2. **`--expect member|management`** — before any declastruct call, read `sts get-caller-identity` + `organizations describe-organization`; refuse (exit 2) unless the account is the org's manager (`management`) or not (`member`). the worst miss it blocks: a member wish applied in the management account lands its resources there, and a global name (an s3 bucket) then needs a full teardown.
3. **`aws.caller.get --env --org --expect member|management`** — the same check, standalone, so a human can prove a slot before a plan.

## .why it cannot be done with `--auth via-ambient` alone

a wish that sources its own slot (`keyrack.source({ org })`) is passed through by keyrack: if AWS_PROFILE is already in the env (the default org's, from `--env`), keyrack returns it as the asked-for org's key. so `--org` must drive the unlock itself, and the guard is the backstop.

## .reference impl

`.agent/repo=.this/role=any/skills/{provision.member,provision.root,aws.caller.get}.sh` in ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-nheuron. on land, that repo drops `provision.member` + `provision.root` for `provision.declastruct --org --expect`.
